title: PHASE A SPACE BASED RE-ENTRY MONITOR - EXPRO+
description: Objectives and TasksThe activity aims to reach a preliminary design for a dedicated mission that will measure from orbit the destructive re-entry of artificial space objects in the Earth's atmosphere by means of a dedicated set of sensors. Pre-cursor sensor level activities haveidentified AlO (aluminium oxide band and associate lithium markers) and SWIR (shortwave infrared) as the most promising and accessible wavelengths from orbit that most re-entry events of artificial will have in common. The study shall establish the system level accommodation of such a sensor suite on a large CubeSat or small satellite platform with capable AOCS suite for pointing and orbit control.As uncontrolled or controlled re-entry events can occur anywhere on the globe, it is envisaged the satelliteplatform shall be in a relatively high orbit to ensure the field of view of the sensors can point to the re-entry streaks generated(which can last for 100'sof km) and preferential observation geometries (such as re-entry event in the Earth shadow) can be reached on average for 1 out of the on average 3 re-entries daily within the forecasting period of a ground segment (roughly two days prior to the event). The mobility needs of the platform shall thus be an integral part of the phase A level tradeoffs.To prepare for the above-described mission, the proposed activity will assess the overall feasibility of the mission and specifically include: Mission and requirements definition: redefine in detail the purpose and mission objectives deriving consistently the satellite system, theorbital, and the groundsegment requirements. These shall be derived from the identified need on regularly observing re-entry events. Conceptual design: based on the mission definition and system requirements, a conceptual design of the satellite will be developed. This includes the basiclayout of the satellite, the platform mass and size, the orbit, the major components and subsystems considering as well launch vehicle, and groundsegment. Definition of the payload (e.g. hyperspectral cameras and SWIR imagers). Identify all critical items (< TRL 6) and derive technology development plans for each including definition of the VV approach. Preliminary cost and schedule: estimate of costs and schedules is developed based on the conceptual design, and the system requirementsto be below 25MEUR. Risk assessment: risks associated with the mission and satellite design will be identified, evaluated, andassessed. Feasibility analysis: the feasibility of the mission and satellite design is assessed, taking into account technical, cost, and schedule considerations. Analysis of the commercialisation opportunities related to the mission concept and the related technologies.

title: HIGH TEMPERATURE HEAT TRANSPORT SYSTEM FOR LUNAR EXPLORATION (HITLUX) - EXPRO+
description: Objective:To develop a high temperature heat transport system for lunar exploration missions, providing an efficientthermal link operating at temperatures in the range of [700degC-1000degC], able to operate within lunarday/night cycles.Description:Sustainable human lunar and planetary exploration relies on effective management of high-temperatureprocesses associated with systems such asIn Situ Resource Utilization (ISRU), regenerative fuel cells, andnuclear and chemical heat generation and storage. The temperatures involved are significantly higher than theclassical ranges considered for the design of thermal control subsystems, reaching values of up to 1000degC.In this context, a high-temperature heat transport system is required to ensure effective temperature control through an efficient thermal link operating in the range of [700degC-1000degC]. The developed technology will be compatible with thelunar environment, including potential operational, stand-by and shutdown cycles associated with the lunar day/night periods. As a target, the technology should also be applicable to similar high-temperature systems operating on Mars.This activity aims to develop a breadboard (BB) of a HIgh Temperature heat transport system for LUnareXploration (HITLUX), serving as a technical demonstrator of the feasibility of this technology. The activity is intended to validate the key driving requirements of the system, including anoperating temperature range from 700degC to 1000degC, a heat transport capability up to 700 W over distances of up to 2 m, and withshutdown and start-up capability.The activity encompasses the following tasks:- Review of the HITLUX requirements and elaborationof a technical specification- Review of the state of the art- Trade-offs of various housing materials and working fluids and concept definition- Thermal analysis of the proposed solution- Design of the breadboard(s) and the associated test bench(s)- Manufacture of breadboard(s) and test bench(s)- Execution of tests and exploitation of results- Thermal model correlation- Conclusions elaboration and roadmap for further technology maturation and de-risking.

title: CAN BACKPLANE INTERFACE MEZZANINE BOARD - EXPRO PLUS
description: To build a mezzanine board to interface with a CAN bus on the units' backplane.Description:As part of the APA (Advanced Power Architecture) initiative, a standardised approach is being developed for internal communication between APA modules within an APA unit. This activity supports that effort by designing a compact, reusable TM/TC interface based on the CAN bus, known for itsreliabilityand simplicity.The mezzanine will serve as a common building block / solution for all APA modules, reducing integration effortandpromoting consistency across designs. By consolidating all required components into a small footprint, it simplifies system architecture, supports modularity and eases procurement, manufacturing and recurrence.This activity focuses on developing a compact mezzanine PCB that integrates five essential components required for CAN-based backplane communication (FPGA or microcontroller, ADC, voltage reference, CAN transceiver and XTAL/oscillator). The goal is to consolidate these elements into a small 30x30 mm footprint, supporting a range of external interfaces and operating on a 3.3V supply.This modular solution aims to simplify internal communication across systems where CAN is the preferred protocol, offering a reusable and scalable interface.This activity encompasses the following tasks:- Consolidate the CAN protocol implementation.- Architecture definition (evaluating if FPGA-based or microcontroller-based).- Identify two suitable options for each one of the 5 required components, prioritising compact packaging and cost.- Design a 30mm x 30 mm PCB accommodating the 5 components and ensuring signal integrity andmanufacturability, ready to be assembled into an APA module and to interface with CAN bus and the APA module.- Implement the software or the VHDL code with the CAN protocol.- Prototyping and testing, assemble and validate the board to confirm functionality and performance.Deliverables: Breadboard,ReportNOTE: This activity is currently in the GSTP Work Plan but will only be implemented after confirmation of financial support from Delegations. The final list of participating states will be known at tender issue.
